name: Bigtha
overview: Bigtha was a male eunuch who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus. He is identified as one of the seven eunuchs who attended to the king, a role indicating a position of trusted service within the royal court. Scripture does not provide further details about his tribe or additional notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Bigtha means "gift of G-d," reflecting a meaningful designation though not explicitly stated as given by God. This proper name highlights a divine association in its meaning, as recorded in Esther 1:10.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Bigtha beyond his role as one of the king's eunuchs. There are no known relatives or connections documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Bigtha's significance lies in his position among the seven eunuchs serving King Ahasuerus, which situates him within the administrative structure of the Persian court. His presence in the narrative underscores the organized and hierarchical nature of the king's household. Although not a central figure, his role contributes to the setting in which key biblical events unfold.
